metric.installation_distribution_experie.candidate_universe: Official Adoptium (the OpenJDK build recommended by dev.java / most-widely-adopted open-source distribution per independent guides) FAQ/docs plus vendor-neutral how-to guides covering all three major OS families (Windows, macOS, Linux) and all three installation paths (native installer, system package manager, version manager) were used as the fixed retrieval route, identical in structure to the route used for every other language's installation metric in this evaluation family.

metric.toolchain_stability_release_matur.candidate_universe: Official Oracle release-notes/support-roadmap pages, the OpenJDK project's own patch-update announcements, and independent vendor (Azul/Adoptium) and press (JRebel, ADTmag, javacodegeeks) coverage of the six-month/LTS cadence were used, matching the fixed retrieval-route structure (official primary source + vendor + independent press) applied to every other language's toolchain-stability metric in this evaluation family.

component_findings.compat_deprecation: Preserved paid evidence (ecosystem-tooling--part-4--java): Strong documented bytecode/class-file backward compatibility, with narrow, disclosed exceptions for preview features and forward-compatibility policy adjustments over time.
component_findings.governance_change: Preserved paid evidence (ecosystem-tooling--part-4--java): Strong documented bytecode/class-file backward compatibility, with narrow, disclosed exceptions for preview features and forward-compatibility policy adjustments over time.
component_findings.release_cadence: Preserved paid evidence (ecosystem-tooling--part-4--java): A predictable, published quarterly (moving toward monthly) security patch cadence is documented and announced far in advance.
component_findings.release_integrity: Preserved paid evidence (ecosystem-tooling--part-4--java): Reproducible, checksum-verifiable artifacts are published across multiple independently maintained vendor builds, with stable download URLs.
component_findings.support_policy: Preserved paid evidence (ecosystem-tooling--part-4--java): Same 6-criterion weighted checklist (100 pts total) applied identically to all 10 languages: (1) documented predictable versioning/release scheme [20], (2) published LTS/support policy with concrete end dates [20], (3) documented backward-compatibility guarantee [20], (4) reproducible, multi-vendor supported build-artifact availability [15], (5) regular maintenance/patch cadence [15], (6) multiple independent vendors providing redundant long-term maintenance [10]. Language age/first-release date is recorded as context only and is not scored.
